source: due2-native, after the external review's R10 (docs/briefings/due2-review-2026-10-24.md): which instant a re-evaluation answers for (decisions/0030)
notes: Authored for due2; no origin result. The four scenarios are the evaluations of one case: the request is asked on 1 March, and the permission's window closes on 1 April. Scenario 1 is the first evaluation, before any payment. Scenario 2 is the same evaluation had the case held a payment made on 15 February; the evaluator sees only occurred_at, so the payment counts whether it was recorded at once or recorded later as an event with an earlier valid_at (workflows §7.1). Scenario 3 is a re-evaluation on 20 April after a payment on 15 April: its request is the case's with at moved to the evaluation's effective_at (decisions/0030), so the closed window makes it NotApplicable. Scenario 4 keeps at at 1 March, which is the review's example: the evaluator answers for the action instant it is given and returns Permit. That is the question about an action on 1 March, which the orchestrator never asks once 1 March has passed (workflows §3.2). Only the due2 profile is selected: due2-core binds odrl:dateTime to due2:actionTime, which is request.at for a rule (due2-profiles.md §3), while DPROD rebinds it to dprod:clock, effective_at (due2-profiles.md §2), under which all four scenarios would test the window at effective_at. The bearer of ex:pay is the request subject, since neither the duty nor its permission names an assignee (due2-workflows.md §5.3).

expected.why: 1 March is before 1 April, so ex:use applies. ex:pay is owed and has no witness, so it is outstanding, and the one route is to perform it: Pending.
ex:use applies at 1 March. ev-pay occurred on 15 February, no later than effective_at, so it is a witness and ex:pay is fulfilled. ex:use is ready: Permit.
The re-evaluation's request has at 20 April, its effective_at, and 20 April is not before 1 April, so ex:use does not apply. No rule applies: NotApplicable, although ev-pay fulfils ex:pay.

scenarios.name: stale request: at 1 March, evaluated 20 April, paid 15 April

expected.why: The window is tested at at, 1 March, so ex:use applies, and ev-pay occurred before effective_at, so ex:pay is fulfilled: Permit.
